- agent-sdk-dev:agent-sdk-verifier-ts: Use this agent to verify that a TypeScript Agent SDK application is properly configured, follows SDK best practices and documentation recommendations, and is ready for deployment or testing. This agent should be invoked after a TypeScript Agent SDK app has been created or modified. (Tools: All tools)
- claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- code-simplifier:code-simplifier: Simplifies and refines code for clarity, consistency, and maintainability while preserving all functionality. Focuses on recently modified code unless instructed otherwise. (Tools: All tools)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- feature-dev:code-architect: Designs feature architectures by analyzing existing codebase patterns and conventions, then providing comprehensive implementation blueprints with specific files to create/modify, component designs, data flows, and build sequences (Tools: Glob, Grep, LS, Read, NotebookRead, WebFetch, TodoWrite, WebSearch, KillShell, BashOutput)

- feature-dev:code-explorer: Deeply analyzes existing codebase features by tracing execution paths, mapping architecture layers, understanding patterns and abstractions, and documenting dependencies to inform new development (Tools: Glob, Grep, LS, Read, NotebookRead, WebFetch, TodoWrite, WebSearch, KillShell, BashOutput)

- feature-dev:code-reviewer: Reviews code for bugs, logic errors, security vulnerabilities, code quality issues, and adherence to project conventions, using confidence-based filtering to report only high-priority issues that truly matter (Tools: Glob, Grep, LS, Read, NotebookRead, WebFetch, TodoWrite, WebSearch, KillShell, BashOutput)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- plugin-dev:agent-creator: Use this agent when the user asks to "create an agent", "generate an agent", "build a new agent", "make me an agent that...", or describes agent functionality they need. Trigger when user wants to create autonomous agents for plugins. Examples:

<example>
Context: User wants to create a code review agent
user: "Create an agent that reviews code for quality issues"
assistant: "I'll use the agent-creator agent to generate the agent configuration."
<commentary>
User requesting new agent creation, trigger agent-creator to generate it.
</commentary>
</example>

<example>
Context: User describes needed functionality
user: "I need an agent that generates unit tests for my code"
assistant: "I'll use the agent-creator agent to create a test generation agent."
<commentary>
User describes agent need, trigger agent-creator to build it.
</commentary>
</example>

<example>
Context: User wants to add agent to plugin
user: "Add an agent to my plugin that validates configurations"
assistant: "I'll use the agent-creator agent to generate a configuration validator agent."
<commentary>
Plugin development with agent addition, trigger agent-creator.
</commentary>
</example> (Tools: Write, Read)

- plugin-dev:plugin-validator: Use this agent when the user asks to "validate my plugin", "check plugin structure", "verify plugin is correct", "validate plugin.json", "check plugin files", or mentions plugin validation. Also trigger proactively after user creates or modifies plugin components. Examples:

<example>
Context: User finished creating a new plugin
user: "I've created my first plugin with commands and hooks"
assistant: "Great! Let me validate the plugin structure."
<commentary>
Plugin created, proactively validate to catch issues early.
</commentary>
assistant: "I'll use the plugin-validator agent to check the plugin."
</example>

<example>
Context: User explicitly requests validation
user: "Validate my plugin before I publish it"
assistant: "I'll use the plugin-validator agent to perform comprehensive validation."
<commentary>
Explicit validation request triggers the agent.
</commentary>
</example>

<example>
Context: User modified plugin.json
user: "I've updated the plugin manifest"
assistant: "Let me validate the changes."
<commentary>
Manifest modified, validate to ensure correctness.
</commentary>
assistant: "I'll use the plugin-validator agent to check the manifest."
</example> (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- plugin-dev:skill-reviewer: Use this agent when the user has created or modified a skill and needs quality review, asks to "review my skill", "check skill quality", "improve skill description", or wants to ensure skill follows best practices. Trigger proactively after skill creation. Examples:

<example>
Context: User just created a new skill
user: "I've created a PDF processing skill"
assistant: "Great! Let me review the skill quality."
<commentary>
Skill created, proactively trigger skill-reviewer to ensure it follows best practices.
</commentary>
assistant: "I'll use the skill-reviewer agent to review the skill."
</example>

<example>
Context: User requests skill review
user: "Review my skill and tell me how to improve it"
assistant: "I'll use the skill-reviewer agent to analyze the skill quality."
<commentary>
Explicit skill review request triggers the agent.
</commentary>
</example>

<example>
Context: User modified skill description
user: "I updated the skill description, does it look good?"
assistant: "I'll use the skill-reviewer agent to review the changes."
<commentary>
Skill description modified, review for triggering effectiveness.
</commentary>
</example> (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob)

- pr-review-toolkit:code-reviewer: Use this agent when you need to review code for adherence to project guidelines, style guides, and best practices. This agent should be used proactively after writing or modifying code, especially before committing changes or creating pull requests. It will check for style violations, potential issues, and ensure code follows the established patterns in CLAUDE.md. Also the agent needs to know which files to focus on for the review. In most cases this will be recently completed work which is unstaged in git (can be retrieved by running git diff). However there can be cases where this is different, make sure to specify this as the agent input when calling the agent. Typical triggers include the user asking for a review of a feature they just implemented, the assistant proactively reviewing its own newly-written code before declaring a task done, and a final pre-PR check before opening a pull request. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:code-simplifier: Use this agent when code has been written or modified and needs to be simplified for clarity, consistency, and maintainability while preserving all functionality. This agent should be triggered automatically after completing a coding task or writing a logical chunk of code. It simplifies code by following project best practices while retaining all functionality. The agent focuses only on recently modified code unless instructed otherwise.

Examples:

<example>
Context: The assistant has just implemented a new feature that adds user authentication to an API endpoint.
user: "Please add authentication to the /api/users endpoint"
assistant: "I've implemented the authentication for the /api/users endpoint. Here's the code:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
Since a logical chunk of code has been written (authentication feature), use the Task tool to launch the code-simplifier agent to improve the code's clarity and maintainability while preserving functionality.
</commentary>
assistant: "Now let me use the code-simplifier agent to refine this implementation for better clarity and maintainability"
</example>

<example>
Context: The assistant has just fixed a bug by adding several conditional checks.
user: "Fix the null pointer exception in the data processor"
assistant: "I've added the necessary null checks to prevent the exception:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
After modifying code to fix a bug, use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the fix follows best practices and maintains code quality.
</commentary>
assistant: "Let me refine this bug fix using the code-simplifier agent to ensure it follows our best practices"
</example>

<example>
Context: The assistant has just refactored a function to improve performance.
user: "Optimize the data sorting algorithm for better performance"
assistant: "I've optimized the sorting algorithm. Here's the updated implementation:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
After completing a performance optimization task, use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the optimized code is also clear and maintainable.
</commentary>
assistant: "Now I'll use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the optimized code is also clear and follows our coding standards"
</example> (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:comment-analyzer: Use this agent when you need to analyze code comments for accuracy, completeness, and long-term maintainability. This includes (1) after generating large documentation comments or docstrings, (2) before finalizing a pull request that adds or modifies comments, (3) when reviewing existing comments for potential technical debt or comment rot, and (4) when you need to verify that comments accurately reflect the code they describe. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:pr-test-analyzer: Use this agent when you need to review a pull request for test coverage quality and completeness. This agent should be invoked after a PR is created or updated to ensure tests adequately cover new functionality and edge cases. Typical triggers include the user asking whether tests on a freshly-created PR are thorough, an updated PR adding new logic that needs coverage analysis, and a final pre-merge double-check before marking a PR ready. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:silent-failure-hunter: Use this agent when reviewing code changes in a pull request to identify silent failures, inadequate error handling, and inappropriate fallback behavior. This agent should be invoked proactively after completing a logical chunk of work that involves error handling, catch blocks, fallback logic, or any code that could potentially suppress errors. Examples:

<example>
Context: Daisy has just finished implementing a new feature that fetches data from an API with fallback behavior.
Daisy: "I've added error handling to the API client. Can you review it?"
Assistant: "Let me use the silent-failure-hunter agent to thoroughly examine the error handling in your changes."
<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>
</example>

<example>
Context: Daisy has created a PR with changes that include try-catch blocks.
Daisy: "Please review PR #1234"
Assistant: "I'll use the silent-failure-hunter agent to check for any silent failures or inadequate error handling in this PR."
<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>
</example>

<example>
Context: Daisy has just refactored error handling code.
Daisy: "I've updated the error handling in the authentication module"
Assistant: "Let me proactively use the silent-failure-hunter agent to ensure the error handling changes don't introduce silent failures."
<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>
</example> (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:type-design-analyzer: Use this agent when you need expert analysis of type design in your codebase. Specifically use it (1) when introducing a new type to ensure it follows best practices for encapsulation and invariant expression, (2) during pull request creation to review all types being added, and (3) when refactoring existing types to improve their design quality. The agent will provide both qualitative feedback and quantitative ratings on encapsulation, invariant expression, usefulness, and enforcement. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- vercel:ai-architect: Specializes in architecting AI-powered applications on Vercel — choosing between AI SDK patterns, configuring providers, building agents, setting up durable workflows, and integrating MCP servers. Use when designing AI features, building chatbots, or creating agentic applications. (Tools: All tools)

- vercel:deployment-expert: Specializes in Vercel deployment strategies, CI/CD pipelines, preview URLs, production promotions, rollbacks, environment variables, and domain configuration. Use when troubleshooting deployments, setting up CI/CD, or optimizing the deploy pipeline. (Tools: All tools)

- vercel:performance-optimizer: Specializes in optimizing Vercel application performance — Core Web Vitals, rendering strategies, caching, image optimization, font loading, edge computing, and bundle size. Use when investigating slow pages, improving Lighthouse scores, or optimizing loading performance. (Tools: All tools)

- zm-implementer: Executes one step of a Zimmermann PWA Kit build plan. Use when a planned step needs to be implemented in code. Writes only the files the step names, and stops rather than expanding scope. (Tools: Read, Write, Edit, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- zm-orchestrator: Scope and spec-conformance checker for an in-flight Zimmermann build. Use after an implementation step to judge whether the work delivers exactly what the plan specified — neither less nor more. Reports a verdict; never edits code. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- zm-planner: Synthesises gathered evidence into an executable build plan for a Zimmermann PWA Kit story. Use after all sources have been gathered, when the findings need to become a sequenced plan with per-step pass criteria. Does not gather evidence itself and does not write code. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, WebFetch)

- zm-scorer: Scores an implemented and tested Zimmermann build step and decides PASS or return-to-implementer. Use after the Tester reports. Judges quality against six axes; never edits code. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- zm-tester: Tests an implemented Zimmermann build step across multiple angles and reports findings. Use after the Implementer reports a step done. Finds and reports problems; never fixes them. Dispatches its own sub-agents for parallel angles. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, Agent)

- zm-orchestrator: Scope and spec-conformance checker for an in-flight Zimmermann build. Use after an implementation step to judge whether the work delivers exactly what the plan specified — neither less nor more. Reports a verdict; never edits code. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)
- zm-planner: Synthesises gathered evidence into an executable build plan for a Zimmermann PWA Kit story. Use after all sources have been gathered, when the findings need to become a sequenced plan with per-step pass criteria. Does not gather evidence itself and does not write code. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, WebFetch)
- zm-scorer: Scores an implemented and tested Zimmermann build step and decides PASS or return-to-implementer. Use after the Tester reports. Judges quality against six axes; never edits code. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)
- zm-tester: Tests an implemented Zimmermann build step across multiple angles and reports findings. Use after the Implementer reports a step done. Finds and reports problems; never fixes them. Dispatches its own sub-agents for parallel angles. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, Agent)

When you launch multiple agents for independent work, send them in a single message with multiple tool uses so they run concurrently.
</system-reminder>

content.text:
## Scale line

I was dispatched one angle only — **data contract fidelity and failure modes** (the 5 sub-items in my brief: schema/consumption fidelity, TS type fidelity, failure-mode tracing, security, migration/install). I ran all 5, plus one live repro script (executed the real `resolveLinkedAssets` against a fabricated response) to convert a hypothesis into a confirmed crash. I did not touch styling, accessibility, AC-compliance-in-general, or re-run the four gates in `gates.md` — none of my findings rest on those numbers, so per the instruction to re-run only what I depend on, I didn't need to and didn't. I stayed out of other reviewers' lanes (no styling/token/a11y commentary beyond what's needed to explain a data-contract finding).

---

## Finding 1 — `unique: true` on `sizeGuide.key` makes the PR's own region-override feature impossible to author

`scripts/contentful/content-types/sizeGuide.js:24`:
```js
validations: [{ regexp: { pattern: '^size-guide__[a-z0-9_]+(__[a-z]{2}_[A-Z]{2})?$' } }, { unique: true }],
```
`unique: true` on a non-localized field is a content-type-wide constraint in Contentful — no two entries of `sizeGuide` may ever share a `key` value, full stop, with no per-region carve-out.

But `overrides/app/hooks/useSizeGuide.ts`'s `pickMostSpecificByRegion` resolution — and its own test suite — requires exactly that: two entries sharing one `key`, differentiated only by `regions`. `overrides/app/hooks/useSizeGuide.test.ts:161-162` (and again `:170-171`, `:180`/`:188`) construct `auEntry`/`globalEntry` (or `localeAuEntry`/`globalDefault`) both keyed `'size-guide__womens_dresses'`. The moment a content editor tries to actually create the second entry this hook and its tests assume is a supported configuration, Contentful will reject the save with a uniqueness violation. The regions-override axis this PR builds and unit-tests is unimplementable in the schema it ships.

Notably, Confluence's own resolution algorithm (ticket.md) never mentions a `regions` axis at all — only `key` + `locale`, two tiers. So `regions` is extra machinery layered on beyond spec, and it's the part that's broken.

- **CONFIRMED** (read the exact validations array against the exact test fixtures; also checked `scripts/contentful/setup/installTemplate.mjs` — it does not strip/transform validations before pushing, so this ships as-is). Not independently verified against a live Contentful space (no CMA token here), but Contentful's `unique` validation has no "except when grouped by another field" mode.
- 🔴 must-fix
- **ONE-OFF** — new content type, no sibling `regions`-scoped type (`footerConfig`, `headerNavigation`) has an analogous unique-constrained lookup key, so this isn't a repeated pattern elsewhere.

## Finding 2 — `imageFallback → asset → file.url` crashes when the linked Image entry resolves but its own Asset doesn't

`overrides/app/pages/product-detail/partials/sizeGuideContent.tsx:412`:
```js
const fallbackAssetUrl = fields.imageFallback?.fields.asset?.fields.file.url;
```
The type (`ImageEntry.fields.asset?: ContentfulAsset`, `ContentfulAsset.fields.file` non-optional) asserts that once `asset` is truthy, `.fields.file.url` is safe. It isn't: `resolveLinkedAssets` (`overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts`, pre-existing, unchanged by this PR) leaves an unresolved Asset Link as a raw stub `{sys:{type:'Link',linkType:'Asset',id}}` — no `.fields` key — whenever that Asset isn't in `includes.Asset` (unpublished/archived/deleted after the `image` entry referencing it was published; Contentful doesn't cascade-restrict this). I reproduced it by executing the real `resolveLinkedAssets` against exactly that shape and evaluating the literal line-412 expression against the result:

```
Resolved imageFallback: { "sys": {"id":"image-1"}, "fields": { ..., "asset": {"sys":{"type":"Link","linkType":"Asset","id":"asset-missing"}} } }
CRASHED with: TypeError - Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'file')
```

No Error Boundary sits anywhere near this render path — a repo-wide search for `ErrorBoundary`/`componentDidCatch` under `overrides/app` found only `zimmAuthDrawerContent`, `checkout-redirect`, `confirmation`, `checkout/partials/payment`. Nothing catches this. No test/story exercises the unresolved-asset shape (`sizeGuideContent.test.ts` only covers pure functions; the `FallbackImage` story's fixture always has a fully-resolved asset).

- **CONFIRMED** by execution, not just static reading.
- 🔴 must-fix
- **UNIFORM** — `overrides/app/utils/resolveImageEntry.ts:24` (`const asset = image?.fields.asset; if (!asset) return undefined;`) has the identical gap: a truthy-but-stub `asset` sails past that guard too. This is a pre-existing, repo-wide contract mismatch between `resolveLinkedAssets`'s asset-branch behaviour and every `ImageEntry.fields.asset` consumer — not unique to this PR's approach. What *is* new here is a third independent reimplementation of the same "resolve ImageEntry → URL" logic instead of reusing `resolveImageEntry.ts` (already shared by `drawer-menu` and `megaMenuContent`) — a DRY miss on top of inheriting the shared bug.

## Finding 3 — Confluence's "no guide (hidden)" fallback isn't hidden anywhere; a Contentful outage looks identical to "no guide"

`overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:1017-1040` builds `pdpDrawerTabs` as a fixed array; the `size-guide` entry has no conditional guard, unlike the `envQualitiesContent` tab two entries below (`:1068`, `...(envQualitiesContent ? [...] : [])`). `pdpDrawerTabs` reaches `<ZimmPdpDrawer tabs={pdpDrawerTabs}>` (`:1344`) unfiltered. For any product with neither a matching `sizeGuide` entry nor a `c_sizeFit` value — including ticket.md's own explicitly-open categories ("Onesize... probably means we do not render a size guide", "Hats content exists... but Hats is NOT in the confirmed allowed-values table") — the shopper still sees a clickable "Size Guide" trigger that opens to a completely empty box (`sizeGuideContent.tsx:429-449`, zero-child `VStack`). Confluence's stated fallback is "no guide (hidden)"; only the *tables-within-the-drawer* are conditional, the tab-trigger itself never is.

Compounding this: `overrides/app/hooks/useSizeGuide.ts:63` destructures only `{ data: entries, isLoading }` (drops `error`), and `product-detail/index.tsx:978` destructures only `{ sizeGuide }` (drops `isLoading` too). A Contentful CDA outage (down/4xx/5xx/malformed JSON) is caught in `useContentful.ts`'s try/catch, sets `error`, and is then silently discarded at both call sites — rendering byte-for-byte identical to "this product has no size guide." No console log, no Sentry breadcrumb. This satisfies "fail independently" (nothing else on the PDP breaks) but blurs "content gap" and "system outage" into one indistinguishable empty state.

- **CONFIRMED** via source read (no `.filter()` anywhere between array construction and the drawer prop).
- 🟡 should-fix
- **ONE-OFF** (specific to this tab array), though the error-swallowing shape (`useContentfulEntries` callers not reading `error`) is worth checking against this PR's own other new call sites — I found none besides this one in the diff.

**Clean, for contrast:** unpublished/missing `sizeGuideTableReference` array entries are handled correctly — `resolveLinkedAssets`'s array branch nulls-and-filters unresolved/cyclic Entry links, and `useSizeGuide.ts`'s `isResolvedTableEntry` re-filters defensively. That section just doesn't render; siblings are unaffected. No finding there.

## Finding 4 — Key-regex vs. Confluence-specified key vs. code construction: a bare-language key can never match

Ticket.md line 36 instructs authoring `size-guide__clothing__en` (bare 2-letter language, no country) as one of the "US variants," alongside `size-guide__clothing__en_CA`. But `useSizeGuide.ts` only ever builds `localeKey = size-guide__{slug}__{canonicalLocale}`, and `canonicalLocale` is always the full `{lang}_{COUNTRY}` form — confirmed every configured storefront locale (`config/sites.overlay.js`, `config/sites.generated.js`) is a 2-part IETF tag (`en-AU`, `en-US`, `en-CA`, `en-GB`, `en-CH`, `en-HK`, `en-AE`), so `.replace('-','_')` always yields e.g. `en_US`, never bare `en`. An entry authored exactly as ticket.md describes is orphaned — never selected by the hook's 2-tier priority — so the "US defaults to inches" override the ticket calls out would silently never apply; US shoppers fall through to the generic default's unit instead. This reads as either a Confluence documentation slip or an unimplemented third tier; I'm not asserting which, just that the two disagree.

- **CONFIRMED** the code can't match a bare-language key; **PLAUSIBLE** (not certain) that this is a real content-authoring trap rather than a doc typo.
- 🟡 should-fix (flag as an open question to the ticket owner)
- **ONE-OFF**

Regex/construction otherwise line up correctly for every other case I checked (`clothing-op-4→size-guide__clothing_op`, `kids→size-guide__kids`, etc., all consistent with `normaliseKey`'s tested behaviour). One low-priority note: `normaliseKey` never lowercases, so if SFCC's actual `c_sizeGuide` attribute value ever has mixed case, every lookup would silently fail — I could not verify actual BM value casing from here (🔵 note, PLAUSIBLE, not confirmed).

## Finding 5 — Schema/field correspondence is otherwise clean; `internalTitle` is declared-but-unread by design, not by accident

Cross-referencing every field in `sizeGuide.js`/`sizeGuideTable.js` against every `.fields.X` access in `useSizeGuide.ts`/`sizeGuideContent.tsx`: no field is read that isn't declared, and no declared field goes unread except `internalTitle` on both types — which matches the established, repo-wide `displayField: 'internalTitle'` editor-only-label convention (`ImageEntry`, `HeaderNavigationEntry`, `NavGroupEntry` all do the same). Not a defect.

One low-severity, non-PR-specific observation: `hasCmInchToggle`/`key`/`internalTitle` are typed non-optional to match `required: true`, but Contentful's `required` is CMS-editorial (blocks *publishing*), not CDA-enforced on every past/future entry. Harmless here because every consumer short-circuits safely on `undefined`. Same category as Finding 2 minus the crash, and it's the same pattern every other content type in `overrides/app/types/contentful.ts` already uses — 🔵 note, not new to this PR, **UNIFORM** but out of this PR's scope to fix alone.

## Finding 6 — Security: clean

No `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` in any new file. `sizeGuideContent.tsx`'s rich-text tables are walked as an AST and emitted as JSX text children (React-escaped); the `sizeFit` HTML string routes through the pre-existing `ZimmProductDescription` → `parseRichText` (`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmProductDescription/index.tsx:3,22`, explicitly "Parsed into React nodes rather than injected as HTML"), not raw-injected. Fallback-image URL construction only fixes protocol-relative `//` → `https://`, with no Contentful-host allowlist — but that's the same trust model every existing `ContentfulAsset` consumer already uses, not a new gap. No token/secret exposure; the CDA delivery token is deliberately public per its own doc comment. **Clean — no findings.**

## Finding 7 — Migration/install step is undocumented and tracked under a different, still-open ticket

`sizeGuide.js`/`sizeGuideTable.js` are auto-discovered by `buildTemplate.js`'s `fs.readdirSync(defsDir)` (confirmed — no registration list to touch), so `npm run sync:contentful` picks them up automatically. But that only updates the org-level EnvironmentTemplate; pushing it into any real environment needs a separate, manual `npm run install:contentful -- --target <env>` (`installTemplate.mjs`, untouched by this diff — confirmed no `unique`/`validations` transform logic in it either, so Finding 1 ships through verbatim). Nothing in this diff documents that install having been run anywhere, and the related ticket SFCC-674 ("Contentful - Size Guide Content Type & Entry Schema (PDP)") is listed in ticket.md as its own ticket, still "Ready For Review" — i.e., tracked as separate, not-yet-done work.

If the content type isn't installed in a given environment, Contentful's CDA is documented to return `200` with an empty `items` array for a nonexistent content type (not an error) — I did not verify this against this org's live space (no credentials here), but if it holds, the feature degrades the same way as Finding 3 (empty-but-present tab) rather than crashing anywhere.

- **CONFIRMED** no install evidence in the diff; **PLAUSIBLE** re: the specific CDA degradation behavior (documented Contentful platform behavior, not independently verified live).
- 🟡 should-fix
- **ONE-OFF**

---

## What I tried to falsify

- Executed the real `resolveLinkedAssets` against a fabricated unresolved-Asset response and ran the literal crash expression from the file — it broke (Finding 2), converting a hypothesis into a repro.
- Checked whether `installTemplate.mjs` strips the `unique:true` validation before pushing, and whether any sibling `regions`-scoped content type has an analogous constraint — neither saves Finding 1.
- Checked for a `.filter()` anywhere between `pdpDrawerTabs`'s construction and its use in `<ZimmPdpDrawer>` — found none, confirming Finding 3.
- Hypothesized a multi-hyphen-locale (`zh-Hant-HK`-style) break in `canonicalLocale` construction, then checked every actually-configured storefront locale in `config/sites.overlay.js`/`sites.generated.js` — all are single-hyphen `en-XX`, so I discarded this as currently unreachable rather than reporting it.
- Checked whether `ZimmProductDescription` (pre-existing, newly exercised here) sanitizes HTML — confirmed it uses AST parsing, not raw injection, so no security finding there.

## What I could not verify

- Whether `sizeGuide`/`sizeGuideTable` are actually installed today in any real Contentful environment (no CMA/CDA credentials in this sandbox).
- Whether Contentful's CDA genuinely returns 200+empty (not an error) for a nonexistent content type in this org's specific space — relying on documented general platform behavior, not a live call.
- Whether BM's SFCC-312 attribute exposure for `c_sizeGuide` is live anywhere today (cross-ticket, no BM access).
- Whether `ZimmPdpDrawer` (untouched by this diff, out of my angle's scope) mounts all tab panels eagerly or only the active one — this affects *when* Finding 2's crash fires (every PDP load for an affected product vs. only once that tab opens), not *whether* it can fire.
- Real BM `c_sizeGuide` attribute value casing (the lowercase-assumption note under Finding 4).

## What Marcel is missing

SFCC-674 ("Contentful - Size Guide Content Type & Entry Schema (PDP)") is a separate, still-open ticket for the same schema this PR ships its own copy of (`sizeGuide.js`/`sizeGuideTable.js`) — worth checking whether SFCC-674's reviewed schema actually matches what's in this PR, since two tickets independently owning "the Contentful schema for size guides" is exactly the shape that produces silent drift (and Finding 1's `unique:true` mistake is the kind of thing a schema-focused review on SFCC-674 might have caught, or might independently disagree with).
